q1: SELECT name FROM drinker WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT f.bar FROM frequents AS f, serves AS s WHERE f.drinker = drinker.name AND f.bar = s.bar AND NOT s.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM likes WHERE drinker = drinker.name))
q2: SELECT f.drinker FROM frequents AS f JOIN serves AS s ON f.bar = s.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = f.bar AND NOT s2.beer IN (SELECT l.beer FROM likes AS l WHERE l.drinker = f.drinker)) GROUP BY f.drinker

explanation: Q1 requires that no bar frequented by the drinker serves a beer not liked by them. Q2 allows the drinker to be included if at least one of their frequented bars serves only liked beers. The difference arises when a drinker frequents multiple bars, one serving only liked beers and another serving some unliked beers.
counterexample_dsp: Drinker Alice frequents Bar1 (serves BeerA and BeerB, both liked) and Bar2 (serves BeerC, not liked). Q1 excludes Alice because Bar2 serves an unliked beer. Q2 includes Alice because Bar1 meets the condition.
